assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance is an original, experimentally unambiguous discovery that became a core device effect (read heads, MRAM, sensors). The MgO coherent-tunnelling step turned a modest effect into a technology, which matters for humanity in the sense the prize requires.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 room-temperature TMR observations by Moodera and Miyazaki were independent and near-simultaneous; Parkin's group (and Yuasa et al.) delivered the large MgO-barrier effect. Three names fit, but the MgO step has other key contributors (e.g. Yuasa, Butler theory) outside the supplied list, and Julliere's 1975 low-temperature result is a historical precursor.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide for three decades and deployed in products; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the credit should split between the 1995 discovery and the MgO giant-TMR step.
Credited names omit people with decisive MgO contributions; I rely on memory for the historical details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a door to a large class of tunable correlated and superconducting phases that could not be reached before. The 2018 experiments by Jarillo-Herrero's group are the original experimental observation and the field has grown quickly.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald 2011 continuum model predicted the flat bands and magic angle; the Jarillo-Herrero group measured correlated insulator and superconductivity in 2018. Theory plus experiment gives a clean configuration, though the Cao and Fatemi co-authors and parallel experiments (Dean, Yacoby, Young) complicate who did what first.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced by many groups, though the microscopic mechanism of superconductivity remains debated and sample-dependence is substantial. Recognition is slightly early but defensible.
uncertainties: Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate the interpretation.
Credit for the experimental side may need to include early-career co-authors not in the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and quantized edge transport link a theoretical prediction to experimental realisations in HgTe quantum wells and magnetically doped films, and have changed how materials are classified. Quantised edge conductance is a clear, verifiable observable.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) predicted the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe wells (with Zhang's prediction as a key link not in this list); Xue's group realised the quantum anomalous Hall effect in 2013. This is a compound discovery in which the three named people fit the theory-to-experiment chain but a fair split with other predictors is contested.
assessment.maturity: Edge-state transport has been confirmed repeatedly, though QAH is still reached only at very low temperatures and applications are not yet realised.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall may deserve distinct recognition.
Key theory contributors (e.g. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Haldane) are not creditable within this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: a laser based on intersubband transitions engineered by band-structure design, working at mid-infrared and terahertz wavelengths that were inaccessible to compact sources. It is demonstrated, widely used in sensing and spectroscopy, and rests on the materials growth I know well.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 Bell Labs demonstration was by Faist, Capasso and colleagues including Sivco and Cho, who supplied the molecular beam epitaxy growth. Capasso, Faist and Cho can be supported, but others at Bell Labs (Sirtori, Hutchinson, Sivco) and earlier Kazarinov-Suris theory complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of continuous development and commercial deployment; very mature.
uncertainties: Kazarinov and Suris predicted intersubband gain in 1971, which complicates priority.
Choice of the third laureate between epitaxy and device co-inventors is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single nitrogen-vacancy centres and coherent control of their spins is a classic instrument-opening discovery, giving atomic-scale sensing of magnetic fields, temperature and strain. The first single-centre experiments are original and clearly verifiable.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group (Gruber et al. 1997) first detected single NV centres optically and Jelezko et al. (2004) showed coherent control of single spins. Two names support the original experiments; Lukin's group developed sensing and quantum-register ideas but is a later step in my reading. I keep the prize to the original experiments.
assessment.maturity: Replicated in many labs and used in nanoscale NMR and biological sensing; sensing applications are still maturing but the core discovery is firm.
uncertainties: Whether the sensing and quantum-network developments deserve inclusion alongside the single-spin discovery.
Overlap with B001 means another candidate may claim part of the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantised conductance in ballistic point contacts, observed in 1988, was a surprising and clean result that opened mesoscopic quantum transport. It is an original experiment whose plateaus can be read directly.
assessment.attribution: Two near-simultaneous papers appeared in 1988: the Delft/Philips group (van Wees, van Houten, Beenakker and co-workers) and the Cambridge group (Wharam, Pepper and co-workers). The named three span both groups, but Wharam and Beenakker are omitted, so the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed for decades and a textbook effect. Recognition is late, which is a risk for living laureates, but not for maturity.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between the Delft and Cambridge groups and junior authors is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty are a major measurement advance, enabling tests of relativity, searches for variations in constants and relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2003) and Ye's group drove it to the lowest uncertainties. Two names are well matched, but Hall and Hansch (frequency combs) were already recognised in 2005 and others contributed to trapped-ion and Sr clocks.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many national laboratories; the redefinition of the second is still pending, so recognition could come with that.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel Prizes for atomic clocks and frequency combs may reduce novelty.
Impact on the SI second is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The two-dimensional electron gas at LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interfaces showed that new electronic phases can appear at atomically engineered oxide boundaries, with superconductivity and gate tunability. It is a discovery very close to my own interface work and interface characterisation by electron microscopy was central.
assessment.attribution: Ohtomo and Hwang reported the 2004 observation; Mannhart's group showed superconductivity and field-effect control. The credit seems clean for these three, though contributions on polar catastrophe theory and on the later role of oxygen vacancies are outside this list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed, but the origin of the carriers (polar discontinuity versus oxygen vacancies and intermixing) is still debated, so interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Carrier origin remains disputed, including oxygen vacancy contributions.
Sample-dependent properties and limited technological use so far.
